description: nf-core/detaxizer samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 1.3.0 schemas. Identifies and optionally removes contaminating sequences from raw data.

classification_bbduk.help: TRUE by curated default, and load-bearing. detaxizer's workflow runs Kraken2 whenever BOTH classifiers are off — Kraken2 is the fallback, not an opt-in. Turning bbduk ON is what keeps Kraken2 out of the DAG and avoids a 64 GB database download.

fasta_bbduk.help: The contaminant sequences bbduk screens against. Points at the LOCAL Luria GRCh38. Leaving this unset while bbduk is on makes the pipeline fall back to iGenomes on S3 — another large download.

classification_kraken2.help: Only set this true if a Kraken2 database is genuinely available. It needs --kraken2db, whose default is a 64 GB remote tarball. Setting it FALSE does not by itself prevent Kraken2 — see classification_bbduk.

kraken2db.help: Required if classification_kraken2 is on. The schema default is a 64 GB S3 tarball, re-downloaded per run. Stage a local copy first; the 8 GB capped Standard database is the smaller option, at the cost of more false negatives.

tax2filter.help: The taxon treated as contamination. Only consulted on the Kraken2 path — bbduk decides by what is in fasta_bbduk.

enable_filter.help: FALSE by curated default: identify first and let a human look before anything is removed from the reads.

validation_blastn.help: Second-pass confirmation with BLAST; builds a database from a FASTA.

pipeline.name: nf-core/detaxizer
pipeline.core_rule: Columns are sample, short_reads_fastq_1, short_reads_fastq_2, long_reads_fastq_1. NOTE the non-standard read column names: this pipeline does NOT use fastq_1/fastq_2. The 1.3.0 schema marks none of them strictly required, but a row with no reads does nothing.
pipeline.reference_requirement: A HUMAN (or other contaminant) reference is required in practice, and which one depends on the classifier. With the curated bbduk path it is the local Luria GRCh38 FASTA via fasta_bbduk — no download. The Kraken2 path instead needs a Kraken2 database (schema default: a 64 GB remote tarball) and is NOT provisioned on Luria. Only `genome` is declared among the usual reference flags at 1.3.0; there is no fasta or gtf param.

validation_rules: The read columns are short_reads_fastq_1 / short_reads_fastq_2, not fastq_1 / fastq_2.

KRAKEN2 IS THE DEFAULT CLASSIFIER. workflows/detaxizer.nf gates it on `(!classification_kraken2 && !classification_bbduk) || classification_kraken2` — so with both flags off it still runs, and stages params.kraken2db, a 64 GB S3 tarball. Setting classification_kraken2=false alone does NOT disable it. Verified the hard way: a run was cancelled 4.2 GB into that download on 2026-08-05.
Keep classification_bbduk true and fasta_bbduk pointed at a local FASTA. That is what keeps Kraken2 out of the DAG.
Do NOT leave fasta_bbduk empty while bbduk is on — the workflow then falls back to getGenomeAttribute('fasta'), i.e. iGenomes on S3.
Do NOT pass --fasta or --gtf: the 1.3.0 schema declares neither.
Keep enable_filter false on a first pass. Identification is reversible; filtering the reads is not.
long_reads_fastq_1 is for long-read libraries; NExtSEEK holds none, so leave it blank.
notes: Applies to any library type, so it is always technically runnable on the 2,057 D.SEQ records we hold. Its natural uses are pre-deposit screening and chasing suspected host or index contamination, and the default action is to REPORT, not remove. IMPORTANT: this pipeline is only cheap on the bbduk path. Its own default is Kraken2 against a 64 GB database, so the curated params here are not cosmetic — they are what makes it runnable without provisioning storage. Confirmed on Luria 2026-08-05.
